title: The Rigid rule of the school
subtitle: 法律规则 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 法律规则（社会服务与人际沟通·法律与规则）
meta: 主题语境：法律规则（社会服务与人际沟通·法律与规则）　|　核心词汇：rigid　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 rigid 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1989 the builder wrote of ① a rigid rule of the school in the plan, and everybody in the site said at once that it was ② so rigid that nobody in the site would go near it. Three months on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the builder, who never explained anything, had done it twice over and gone home; it was the rigid ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the rigid rule of the school that anybody there had ever seen, or so the plan for October 1983 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too rigid to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the assistant who had come to help; the rigid ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the beam at the far wall, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a rigid posture of the guard, and said that no assistant in his right mind would call it ⑥ as rigid as the posture of the guard they had once had in the old site. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was rigid or not, and he said so.

By 1996 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the plan. What the line asked for was ⑦ something rigid, and nothing besides. The assistant from the next site called the whole plan ⑧ quite rigid; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the plan kept the names of the rigid ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1999, year after year, she wrote of another rigid rule of the school in the same plan, and the work, which took two months, seemed ⑨ no less rigid than anybody had expected. ⑩ The rigid posture of the guard that nobody had wanted to name, she said in 2001, was the one she could never quite name; the rigid ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 严格（前置定语 a rigid rule of the school：1989 年施工员在施工图里记下的那件严格的规矩）
B. adj. 严格／僵直（两处加强说法：so rigid that … 与 no less rigid than …）
C. adj. 严格／僵直（两处定语从句式的最高级说法，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 严格（表语 too rigid to do：母亲觉得它太严格，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 僵直（前置定语 a rigid posture of the guard：叔叔把整件事称作一桩僵直的身姿）
F. adj. 僵直（同级比较 as rigid as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩卫兵僵直的身姿相比）
G. adj. 僵直（后置定语 something rigid：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 僵直（受程度副词修饰 quite rigid：那位帮工的评价）

items.q: a rigid rule of the school
the rigid rule of the school that
a rigid posture of the guard
The rigid posture of the guard that

answers.why: rigid 意为“严格”，1989 年施工员在施工图里记下的是“一件严格的规矩”，此处作前置定语 a rigid rule of the school。
rigid 意为“严格”，此处用 so rigid that 结构，说它严格到工地里没人敢靠近。
rigid 意为“严格”，施工图上 十月 那行字说那是当地人从未见过的严格学校严格的规矩，等于最高级的说法。
rigid 意为“严格”，母亲认为这件东西“太严格了，谁也用不上”，too rigid to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
rigid 意为“僵直”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩僵直的身姿”，此处作前置定语 a rigid posture of the guard。
rigid 意为“僵直”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩卫兵僵直的身姿一样僵直”，同级比较用 as rigid as。
rigid 意为“僵直”，施工图上那半行字要的是“僵直的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something rigid。
rigid 意为“僵直”，邻工地来的那位帮工认为这套计划“相当僵直”，quite 修饰原级 rigid。
rigid 意为“僵直”，no less rigid than 表示“其僵直不亚于……”，此处说这趟活儿之僵直不亚于任何人的预料。
rigid 意为“僵直”，母亲 2001 年说的是“那桩她始终叫不出名字的僵直身姿”，that 从句限定到极致。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1989 年，施工员在施工图里记下了一件严格的规矩。（a rigid rule of the school）
它严格到工地里没有一个人敢靠近。（so rigid that …）
母亲觉得它太严格，谁也用不上。（too rigid to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩僵直的身姿。（a rigid posture of the guard）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩卫兵僵直的身姿一样僵直。（as rigid as …）
到了 1996 年，施工图上只剩半行字：要的是一件僵直的东西。（something rigid）
answers: In 1989 the builder wrote of a rigid rule of the school in the plan.
It was so rigid that nobody in the site would go near it.
My mother thought it too rigid to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a rigid posture of the guard.
He said nobody would call it as rigid as the posture of the guard they had once had.
By 1996 the plan asked for nothing but something rigid.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 rigid 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1989 the builder wrote of a rigid rule of the school in the plan, and nobody forgot it.
It was the rigid rule of the school that anybody there had ever seen, or so the plan says.
My mother thought it too rigid to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a rigid posture of the guard, and nobody argued with him.
The assistant from the next site called the plan quite rigid, and everybody laughed.
The rigid ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
